Series::floor¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::floor() const -> Series
Series& Series::floor_()

What It Does¶

floor() rounds each element downward to the greatest integer value that is less than or equal to that element.

For positive numbers, that often reads like “drop the fraction.” For negative numbers, it is more important to think in terms of order on the number line: the result moves toward negative infinity.

Returns¶

Series A new Series whose elements have been rounded downward.

Gradient¶

Away from integer boundaries, floor(x) is piecewise constant, so its local derivative is 0.

That means a scalar objective built from floor() does not propagate ordinary value sensitivity through those lanes on the current reverse-mode surface.

In-Place Form¶

floor_() is the in-place sibling of floor(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.7, -1.2});

auto& ref = x.floor_();
std::cout << "x=" << x << "\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "same object: " << (&ref == &x);

Output¶

x=pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[1, -2]
same object: true

Examples¶

Example 1. floor() rounds toward negative infinity, which matters most for negative inputs.

pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::make_series({
    {-1.2, -0.1, 0.0},
    {1.2, 2.9, 3.0},
}).floor());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ -2.0000 -1.0000 0.0000 ⎤
⎣  1.0000  2.0000 3.0000 ⎦

Example 2. Reverse-mode sensitivity is zero through the rounded output in the usual non-boundary case.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-1.2, 0.0, 3.8});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

auto y = x.floor();
y.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "out=" << y << "\n";
std::cout << "dL_dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

out=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-2, 0, 3]
dL_dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 0, 0]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • floor() is not “truncate the decimals” for negative values.

  • Values already at an integer stay unchanged.

  • The transform has jump discontinuities at integers.

Summary¶

Use floor() when values must be rounded downward in the mathematical sense, not merely shortened toward zero.

See Also¶

  • Series::ceil: the upward counterpart.

  • Series::round: nearest-integer rounding.

  • Series::trunc: fractional-part removal toward zero.
